summary: Tucked into a narrow canyon at the base of Mount Tamalpais, Larkspur packs an almost improbable amount of geographic drama into just 3.2 square miles — redwood-shaded creek corridors open abruptly onto a compact downtown of restaurants and shops along Magnolia Avenue, then give way to salt marshes edging the bay. The Golden Gate Ferry terminal at the eastern edge connects directly to San Francisco's Financial District, making this a textbook bedroom community where the commute is actually a scenic boat ride rather than a freeway grind. That said, the affordability math is stark: the median home value of roughly $1.8 million lands at about 13.4 times the median household income of $134,744, placing ownership firmly out of reach at the median earnings level even with substantial savings, while median rent near $2,867 per month consumes roughly a quarter of that same income — manageable but not cheap. Daily highs averaging 66°F year-round and nearly nine hours of sunshine per day mean mild, dry summers and cool but rarely cold winters, ideal for the extensive trail network climbing into the open space above town. Larkspur is a place where the landscape constantly upstages the real estate prices — until you check them.
